narrative_purpose: Establishes the chapter's central ratio in one image: the entire product of a hunt is a container a person can hold in one hand, and the animal it came from fills the background.
subject: A gloved human hand at the centre of the frame holding up a small double-walled cylindrical glass vial about the size of a thermos, filled with a viscous luminous golden-yellow fluid that catches the light as it tilts. Behind the hand, past a wet steel deck railing, the vast dark flank of a dead marine animal rises out of the water, so large it fills the whole background and its edges run past the frame. A heavy drill unit hangs from a crane arm at the top of the frame, still and dripping.
scene: The wet working deck of an ocean vessel, steel plating underfoot, sea beyond the railing.
camera: Close waist-height shot on the hand and vial, the animal's flank filling the background out of focus.
light: Cold overhead deck lamps on the steel, warm amber glow from within the vial itself, deep shadow across the animal's flank.
palette: Void indigo shadow, cold grey wet steel, one concentrated warm amber-gold source in the vial.
style: Painterly naturalist plate, close and material, not a product photograph.
detail_level: Crisp on the glove, the vial and its fluid; the animal's flank soft and dark; open dark space upper left for callouts.
composition: Hand and vial slightly right of centre at mid-height, dark flank filling the right and lower background, open dim deck space at upper left and lower left for overlay labels.
consistency_notes: The fluid is luminous golden-yellow and viscous, glowing from inside the glass. The animal reads as immense and recently dead but is shown as flank and silhouette only, never as a wound.
negative_prompt: no text, no labels, no arrows, no logos, no photographic or 3D-render look, no cartoon style, no explicit gore or open wounds
